title: Inessive demonstratives review
focus: Mix singular and plural inessive demonstratives in independent and noun-modifying use.

exercises.prompt: Context: Three garages are visible. Both people refer to the garage they identified earlier. Choose the sentence that means “The car is in it.” Beside a noticeboard. Start from se (“that or it, already identifiable”). Use the supplied subject auto (“car”).
exercises.explanation: Siinä is the inessive form of se and expresses a bounded inside or immediately located relation.

sentenceExplanation.translation: The car is in it.
sentenceExplanation.pattern: subject being located + linking verb + inessive demonstrative location

Correct. Siinä is the inessive form of se and expresses a bounded inside or immediately located relation.
“tässä” is the singular inessive form linked to tämä; use “siinä”, the singular inessive form linked to se.
“tuossa” is the singular inessive form linked to tuo; use “siinä”, the singular inessive form linked to se.
“se” is a singular nominative form for an already identifiable non-human referent; use “siinä”, the singular inessive form linked to se.
